record.original_question: If G is a connected n-vertex m-edge graph minimizing lambda(G) - d(G) among all connected graphs with those parameters, must the degree spread satisfy Delta(G) - delta(G) <= 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 5 (Hong [84]). Let G ∈ H(n, m) be a connected graph minimizing λ(G) − d(G). Is it true that Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ 1 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple connected graph on n vertices with m edges. Let A(G) be its adjacency matrix and let λ(G) denote its largest eigenvalue (spectral radius). Let d(G) = 2m/n denote the average degree of G, and let Δ(G) and δ(G) denote the maximum and minimum degrees, respectively. Let H(n,m) be the family of all connected graphs with exactly n vertices and m edges.

Suppose G* ∈ H(n,m) minimizes the quantity λ(G) − d(G) over all G ∈ H(n,m). Must G* be almost regular, i.e., must it satisfy

  Δ(G*) − δ(G*) ≤ 1 ?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (attributed to Hong, 1993) asks whether minimizers of the spectral radius (equivalently λ(G) − d(G) for fixed n, m) among connected graphs in H(n,m) must be almost regular. Recent work (e.g., 2024 paper on the minimum spectral radius of connected graphs of given order and size) verifies the conjecture affirmatively for various ranges of (n, m) and exhibits the extremal graphs in many cases, but a complete resolution for all (n, m) does not appear in the literature, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the minimum spectral radius of connected graphs of given order and size
status_evidence.snippet: Hong asked if it is true that among all connected graphs of given number of vertices n and number of edges e, the graphs having minimum spectral radius must be almost regular. We answer this affirmatively for various values of n and e.
status_evidence.claim: Hong's question is answered affirmatively for various values of (n,e), but not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: An Optimization Approach to Degree Deviation and Spectral Radius
status_evidence.snippet: Relates degree deviation and spectral radius, building on Hong-type problems.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on Hong's spectral-radius/degree problems indicates the question remains a topic of ongoing investigation.
